metadata.description: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the Seed action library. scripts/seed/seed_action_library.js reads this file and computes points from effort/frequency/impact at seed time -- it no longer carries an inline action array. Every shipping action lives here.
metadata.methodology: Values cross-referenced from 2-3 tier-1 sources minimum. Conservative estimates used when sources disagree.

grid_factors.source: Ember, Global Electricity Review 2026 (2025 world average, CO2e)
grid_factors.note: Superseded the retired 386 g CO2/kWh on 2026-08-02 (decision E1). Regional factors are a separate open question -- see Plan/PDR_GRID_REGIONALISATION.md.

primary_sources: UK DEFRA Greenhouse Gas Conversion Factors 2024/2025
US EPA Greenhouse Gas Equivalencies Calculator
metadata.points_formula: max(1, round(co2_grams^0.4 * effortMult * rarityMult * impactMult)); constants in scripts/seed/seed_action_library.js

actions.name_ja: 高インパクトの食事をスキップ
actions.description_en: Choose a plant-based meal instead of beef or lamb today
actions.description_ja: 今日は牛肉やラム肉の代わりに植物性の食事を選択する
actions.description_es: Elegir una comida vegetal en vez de carne de res o cordero hoy
actions.calculation_notes: Covers beef and lamb, so it binds to the SMALLER implied saving and the reward is honest whichever the user skipped. Lamb 39.72 kg CO2e/kg (OWID / Poore & Nemecek 2018 grapher, 'Lamb & Mutton,2010,39.72') per 100 g serving = 3972 g. Minus the standardized plant-alternative baseline of 200 g CO2e per 100 g serving (beans/lentils, OWID 'Other Pulses' mean 1.79 kg/kg = 179 g, rounded up to 200 g; the same baseline every meatless action uses) = 3772 g. Rounded down to 3700 g (savings always round DOWN). Beef implies 6836 g on the same basis; crediting that for a lamb skip would overstate by 80%. Same minimum-of-covered-items rule as plant_milk.

sources.quote: Beef (dairy herd),2010,33.3

sources.name: Our World in Data, Less meat is nearly always better than sustainable meat
sources.quote: Around 56% of global beef production comes from dedicated beef herds; and 44% from dairy herds.

sources.name: Our World in Data FAQ
sources.quote: On one chart you previously showed a value of 99.5 kilograms CO2eq per kilogram of beef from beef herds. On another, it was shown as 60 kgCO2eq per kilogram. Why were these values different? ... The former showed the mean, and the latter the median. This is how the data is made available in the underlying study from Poore and Nemecek (2018). ... We updated the data on the breakdown of emissions on 15th June 2022 based on supplementary data provided by the author, with supply chain losses included, and given as the mean. This means these two charts are now consistent.

Chicken 9.87 kg CO2e/kg (OWID / Poore & Nemecek 2018 grapher, 'Poultry Meat,2010,9.87') per 100 g serving = 987 g. Minus the standardized plant-alternative baseline of 200 g CO2e per 100 g serving (beans/lentils, OWID 'Other Pulses' mean 1.79 kg/kg = 179 g, rounded up to 200 g; the same baseline every meatless action uses) = 787 g. Rounded down to 780 g (savings always round DOWN). Pork implies 1031 g on the same basis; the retired per-item pork action shipped 1000 g and is kept in research_only_records. Same minimum-of-covered-items rule as plant_milk.

The action names plant milks generically, so it binds to the SMALLEST implied saving across the shipped plant milks -- soy 543 g, not oat 562 g. Ships 460 g, deliberately below that bound and unchanged through the 2026-07 correction pass; a silent change here is a points-economy change.

actions.name_ja: フードデリバリーをスキップ
actions.description_en: Cook at home instead of ordering food delivery today

actions.description_es: Cocinar en casa en vez de pedir delivery de comida hoy
actions.calculation_notes: NOT CO2-CLAIMABLE, shipped at 0 g 2026-08-09. The peer-reviewed comparison runs the other way: delivered meal kits beat grocery-store meals by 2.0 kg CO2e/meal, and last-mile emissions are LOWER for delivery (-0.45 kg CO2e/meal) because a van route amortizes across many drops while a store trip is one car. Restaurant delivery is not the same system as a meal kit, but no primary supports a saving for cooking at home, so the previous 600 g had no basis. Ships as a habit prompt worth 0 g until a restaurant-delivery LCA exists.

sources.name: Heard, Bandekar, Vassar & Miller, 'Comparison of Life Cycle Environmental Impacts from Meal Kits and Grocery Store Meals', Resources, Conservation and Recycling 147 (2019)
sources.quote: grocery meal greenhouse gas emissions are 33% higher than meal kits (8.1 kg CO2e/meal compared with 6.1 kg CO2e/meal kit)

actions.calculation_notes: White fish 5.1250386 kg CO2e/kg: Gephart et al. 2021 Bayesian meta-analysis of seafood ('Environmental performance of blue foods') via Our World in Data, the `white_fish` item in data/app/food_items.json. Per 150 g fillet = 769 g. Minus the standardized plant-alternative baseline of 200 g CO2e per 100 g serving (beans/lentils, OWID 'Other Pulses' mean 1.79 kg/kg = 179 g, rounded up to 200 g; the same baseline every meatless action uses) = 569 g. Rounded down to 560 g (conservative; savings always round DOWN). Re-based 2026-08-08: the seafood source decision retired the assembled fish_wild 9.5 this action previously used, and the reward fell 1200 -> 560 g with it.

actions.description_en: Refuse disposable cutlery with takeaway or delivery today

actions.calculation_notes: Re-scoped 2026-08-09 from 'straws, cutlery, napkins' to cutlery alone. The old wording forced a bind to its smallest item -- a PP straw at 1.7 g -- which made the reward not worth shipping; the previous 15 g fitted neither item. Peer-reviewed LCA, functional unit '1-time use of cutlery fork/spoon', cradle-to-grave: PS cutlery 0.0514 kg CO2e at 100% incineration, rounded down to 51 g. END-OF-LIFE SENSITIVITY: the same paper gives 0.032 kg for landfill and 0.0119 kg for recycling, a 4.3x spread. Incineration ships because Japan, the primary market, incinerates most plastic waste; in a high-recycling market this action is worth ~12 g.

sources.name: Chaudhari et al., 'Life Cycle Assessment of Selected Single-Use Plastic Products', Sustainability 14(21):14170 (2022)
sources.quote: the total GWP impact of PS cutlery is 0.0514 kg CO2 (eq) for 100% incineration

actions.calculation_notes: DENIM BASIS -- this value is a pair of jeans, not an average garment. Levi's own ISO 14040/14044 panel-reviewed LCA of the 501: 33.4 kg CO2e cradle-to-grave, of which consumer care is 37% and end of life 3%, both unavoidable whether the garment is new or secondhand. The production a buyer actually avoids is fiber 9% + fabric 27% + cut/sew/finish 8% + sundries and packaging 5% = 49% of 33.4 = 16.3 kg. Ships 15 kg, below that, on the same one-for-one displacement assumption as used_car_purchase (see notes.avoided_emissions_caveat). A cotton tee's production is several times lower, so this is generous for light garments. Next pass: source a light-garment LCA and bind to the minimum, as the food tier actions do.

1.description: No Poverty - systemic issue, indirect actions

actions: ALL transport, food, energy, recycling actions

notes.regional_variation: Energy-related actions vary significantly by grid carbon intensity. US average 0.37 kg/kWh, UK 0.21 kg/kWh, France 0.05 kg/kWh. Consider allowing user input.
notes.food_caveat: Transport accounts for only 5-6% of food emissions. 'Eat local' has limited impact compared to 'eat less beef'.
notes.reusable_items_caveat: Cotton bags require 7,100+ uses to break even. Recommend polypropylene bags (10-45 uses breakeven).
notes.growing_vegetables_caveat: University of Michigan 2024 found urban agriculture has 6× higher emissions than conventional farming due to infrastructure. Exception: tomatoes grown outdoors vs greenhouse.
notes.flight_radiative_forcing: DEFRA uses 1.9× multiplier for non-CO2 aviation effects. Some scientists argue 2.7-3× is more accurate.
notes.avoided_emissions_caveat: Actions that credit avoided manufacturing (used_car_purchase, secondhand_clothing, repair_item, borrow_instead_buy, donate_items) are COUNTERFACTUAL claims, not inventory accounting. Each scores one decision against what would otherwise have been produced; they are not a share of any physical object's embodied carbon. Two consequences. (1) They are not additive: if a car is built, sold, and resold, the manufacturing happened once, and crediting each buyer is only coherent because each buyer faced a separate buy-new decision -- never sum them and never present the total as a physical quantity of CO2 not emitted. (2) They assume one-for-one displacement, which is an upper bound: real markets displace less than one new unit per secondhand purchase, and no published rate exists to correct with. The methodology screen must say both.

research_only_records.why: Research records from the pre-2.0 database that have no shipping action. Kept for provenance: the transport-mode swaps are now handled by the transport calculator's logging bridge rather than by discrete actions, and the rest were researched but never shipped. Do NOT seed these -- seed_action_library.js reads `actions` only.
